body:
<!-- pr-reviewer: ea51a4b2b22c7832dd957cdb143d4286a78cce10 -->

Ready for the maintainer to merge.

What looks good
- Std-only file lock (`File::try_lock`); no new dependency; one new module (`link_owner.rs`) and one rule at two call sites; the whole class of "a stale or unproved link file is dialed" is covered.
- The CLI dials only a file whose window is proved alive, before the hello and after it; a free lock removes the stale files and never dials; a file with no lock to test is skipped with the reason; no silent fall-back.
- The post-hello check closes the gap where the window ends during the exchange; the pinning test for that case is strong and deterministic.
- The new test file sits in the existing `mcp_live` directory suite; the gate map names `link_owner`; the provenance line and the decision record are present; files stay under the 400-line line.

Results (self-hosted runner: https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/actions/runs/45644091879 - trial merge clean on main 138a592a196a6c68e8608b560fbd2696977a71c7; quick gate: 167 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled, wall 18.9 min; clippy `-p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean).
- Local light lane, trial-merged with current main (49bfcaea): 6 steps, 0 failed, wall 20.6 min (release, sccache).
- Example catalog: not run - no post or toolpath changed (the diff touches only the MCP link).
- No heavy step: this is a P3 PR, not a safety-floor PR.
- Windows and macOS were not built or run (disclosed in the body); the `#[cfg(unix)]` addition is unix-only and does not change a Windows reading.

Requested before merge: none.

Notes (not blocking)
1. The window removes the lock file in `Drop` while it still holds it (crates/app/src/mcp/link.rs:246-260). On Windows (`LockFileEx`) an open locked file cannot be deleted, so the removal may fail and the `.lock` file may linger (the error is caught and logged, and the next CLI run removes the stale file, so this is cosmetic). The body's claim "The window removes the lock file with its link file when it closes" may not hold on Windows. Windows was not exercised; dropping the file handle before the removal (for example an `Option<File>` field taken in `Drop`) would make the claim true there.
2. The PR body ends with `Fixes #3995` (per the maintainer's decision) but the commit message ends with `Refs #3995`. The issue closes via the PR body, and force-push is forbidden, so this is cosmetic - but the commit could read consistently if the branch is rebased by a contributor.
3. The test `false_server_on_stale_entry_is_refused_with_no_tool_calls_sent` (crates/app/tests/mcp_live/ui_link.rs:225) now holds a live lock, so a file it writes is no longer stale; the name says "stale entry" for a case that is no longer stale. Cosmetic.
4. The body's "What stays open" section says "Thus this PR uses `Refs #3995`" while the final line says `Fixes #3995`; the maintainer's comment explains the change. Cosmetic.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
